title: Bank data platform
text:
# Bank data platform

An end-to-end analytics engineering pipeline on real retail-banking data: checksum-verified ingestion, a dbt star schema on DuckDB (Snowflake-ready), a blocking quality gate, refresh-over-refresh QC, alerting, and the same pipeline orchestrated two ways, in Airflow and in Dagster.

The data is the PKDD'99 Czech bank dataset: 4,500 accounts, 5,369 clients, 682 loans and 1,056,320 transactions from 1993 to 1998. It's one of the few public datasets with a real bank ledger, and it is messy in the ways real banking data is.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Stack** | Python 3.12, dbt Core 1.12, DuckDB, Airflow 3.4 (Docker), Dagster 1.13, GitHub Actions, SQLFluff, Ruff, pytest, uv |
| **dbt project** | 19 models, 121 data tests, 2 unit tests, 3 seeds, 8 sources, 1 exposure, 2 enforced contracts |
| **Quality** | 8 gate checks (block or alert), refresh-over-refresh QC, 17 Python tests, including one that proves incremental builds equal a full rebuild |
| **Runs** | `make run` for one build, `make replay` for twelve simulated monthly refreshes |
| **Assistant** | A Streamlit chatbot that answers questions about this project from its own docs and code (`chatbot/`), built for Hugging Face Spaces |

title: Architecture
text:
## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR src[(GitHub mirror
pinned commit)] -->|ingest: download,
SHA-256 lock| landing[/landing files/] landing -->|load: all text,
as-of replay| raw[(raw)] raw --> gate{quality gate
8 checks} gate -- BLOCK --> stop[stop: marts keep
last good build] gate -- pass / ALERT --> stg[staging
8 views] stg --> int[intermediate
sequenced ledger,
account parties] int --> core[core
dims + facts] core --> risk[risk
loan book] core --> rep[reporting
monthly KPIs] rep --> qc{refresh QC
vs last refresh} qc --> alerts([Slack / email /
alert log]) gate -. alerts .-> alerts ``` Each step is a plain Python module with a CLI (`pipeline/`). Airflow, Dagster, CI and `make` all call the same code, so the pipeline behaves the same however it's triggered. | Layer | Schema | What it holds | |---|---|---| | Landing | files | Source TSVs, verified against `pipeline/sources.lock.json` | | Raw | `raw` | Exact copy of each file, every column as text, plus load metadata and an audit table | | Staging | `staging` | One view per source table: typed, renamed and decoded, with blank, padded and NULL codes normalized | | Intermediate | `intermediate` | `int_transactions_sequenced` (recovered posting order) and `int_account_parties` (one row per account) | | Core | `core` | `dim_date`, `dim_district`, `dim_client`, `dim_account`, `fct_transactions` (incremental), `fct_account_monthly` (periodic snapshot) | | Risk | `risk` | `fct_loans` (contract enforced), `mart_loan_portfolio` | | Reporting | `reporting` | `mart_monthly_kpis` (contract enforced), the board-pack table the QC watches |

title: The hardest problem: recovering the order of the ledger
text:
## The hardest problem: recovering the order of the ledger

The source has no posting time, and transaction ids aren't chronological within a day. Ordering each account by `(date, id)` and checking that `previous balance + amount = reported balance` breaks on **524,126 of 1,051,820 steps (49.8%)**.

Profiling showed the bank posted credits before debits within a day, and that the reported balance itself encodes the order: credits raise it and debits lower it. `int_transactions_sequenced` orders by date, then direction, then the balance path:

```sql
row_number() over (
    partition by account_id
    order by
        posted_on,
        case when amount >= 0 then 0 else 1 end,                         -- credits first
        case when amount >= 0 then balance_after else -balance_after end, -- follow the balance
        transaction_id
)
```

That leaves **13 breaks in 1.05M (0.001%)**: same-day ties that the data alone can't order. The continuity test (`tests/assert_balance_continuity.sql`) warns on any break and fails the build only above 0.01%, which would mean the logic or the source changed. Each step tolerates one cent, because the mirror rounded amounts and balances separately when it rescaled them.

The model is incremental. Each run re-sequences a 7-day lookback window and anchors it on the last balance already sequenced before the window. `tests/test_incremental_equivalence.py` builds two months incrementally, rebuilds from scratch and asserts that both tables are identical, hash for hash.

title: Data quality, in layers
text:
## Data quality, in layers

**1. At extract.** Files come from a pinned commit and must match a committed SHA-256 lock. A changed upstream file is deleted from landing and the run stops, rather than quietly changing every number downstream.

**2. The quality gate, before any model runs** (`pipeline/quality_gate.py`). Each check either blocks or alerts:

| Check | Severity | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| G01 every raw table has rows | BLOCK | An extract or load that failed silently |
| G02 transaction ids unique | BLOCK | Duplicated postings that would double money downstream |
| G03 dates and amounts parse | BLOCK | A changed file layout |
| G04 every posting has an account | BLOCK | Orphans that would drop out of account-level marts |
| G05 no closed month empty | BLOCK | A missed partition |
| G06 feed is current | ALERT | A stale feed |
| G07 volume band (±25% of the six-month median) | ALERT | Large drifts |
| G08 blank category share | ALERT | A broken upstream code mapping |

A failed block exits non-zero, the orchestrator skips everything downstream, and the marts keep the last good build: stale, but not wrong. Every result lands in `dq.check_results`. To let one known issue through on purpose, an owner adds a row to `dq.gate_bypass`. A check that can't measure anything fails if it's a block check, because "couldn't verify" isn't "verified".

title: Data quality, in layers
text:
**3. dbt tests on every layer** (121 data tests and 2 unit tests): keys and grain, relationships, accepted values, sign rules, loan arithmetic (`principal = term × payment`), and reconciliations written as a reusable generic test, `reconciles_with`. Every layer reconciles to the one before it, and the published fact reconciles to raw, month by month, on row count and money. Marts that feed reporting have enforced contracts, so a refactor can't silently rename or retype a reported column.

**4. Refresh-over-refresh QC, after the build** (`pipeline/refresh_compare.py`). Tests prove a build is internally consistent. They can't tell you that a number the board saw last month has changed. After every run, the QC step snapshots `mart_monthly_kpis` and compares it with the previous refresh:

- **RESTATED**: a month published last time has a different value now
- **DROPPED**: a month published last time is missing
- **OUT_OF_BAND**: the newest month moved more than 25% against the month before

It writes a Markdown report to `reports/qc/` and alerts. Replaying monthly refreshes finds zero restatements, as it should for closed months, and it correctly flags March 2016, when debits rose 27% month over month.

**5. Alerting** (`pipeline/notify.py`). Gate failures, dbt failures, QC findings and Airflow task failures go to Slack or email when those are configured, and always to `logs/alerts.jsonl`. A failed send is logged, never raised: an alert problem must not take the pipeline down.

title: What the checks caught while building this
text:
### What the checks caught while building this

- **Orphan standing orders.** When the replay first ran, a relationship test failed: standing orders were loaded for accounts that didn't exist yet at that date. Fix: account-dependent tables now enter the extract with their account.
- **A mart test running in the staging step.** dbt's default eager test selection ran a mart's reconciliation against last month's mart during the staging build. Fix: `--indirect-selection cautious`.
- **A wrong assumption about clients.** An age test with a minimum of 10 failed on real eight-year-olds: junior-account disponents. The data was right and the threshold was wrong. Thresholds should come from the domain, not from intuition.
- **The gate crashing on an empty window.** A unit test showed the volume check returned no row before the first closed month. That led to the rule above: a block check that can't measure fails.

title: Messy data, handled in staging
text:
## Messy data, handled in staging

- Code columns mix padded (`"  "`), blank and NULL values for "no value". The `clean_code` macro normalizes all three to NULL.
- District 69 has no 1995 unemployment or crime figures. They stay NULL, not zero.
- Amounts are signed (credits positive, debits negative); a test enforces the sign against the transaction type.
- Czech source codes are decoded through a seed that keeps the original Czech value alongside the English description.

title: Replaying a live feed
text:
## Replaying a live feed

The dataset is static, but production data arrives in increments. `pipeline.load --as-of DATE` emits only the rows whose business date is on or before that day, like an extract taken on that date. Airflow's monthly schedule with catchup turns the dataset into 36 monthly refreshes, so the incremental models, freshness checks and refresh QC behave as they would on a live source.

Known limit: loan status is the status at the end of the source period, so a replayed extract sees each loan's final status from the day it's granted.

title: Running it
text:
## Running it

Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Docker is needed for Airflow only.

```bash
make setup     # install
make run       # download, load, gate, build, test, QC
make replay    # twelve monthly refreshes of 2018
make test-all  # unit tests and incremental equivalence
make docs      # dbt docs and lineage at localhost:8081
make dagster   # Dagster UI at localhost:3000
make airflow   # Airflow UI at localhost:8080
```

Without `make`, run `uv run python -m pipeline.run --full-refresh`. To point dbt at Snowflake, set the `SNOWFLAKE_*` variables and `DBT_TARGET=snowflake`. The SQL uses dbt's cross-database macros so it compiles on both; the Snowflake target isn't exercised in CI.

title: Orchestration
text:
### Orchestration

- **Airflow** (`orchestration/airflow/`): a monthly DAG with catchup over 2016 to 2018. The six tasks are `ingest`, `load_raw`, `quality_gate`, `dbt_staging`, `dbt_marts` and `refresh_qc`. The pipeline runs in its own virtualenv inside the image, so dbt and Airflow dependencies never clash. `max_active_runs=1`, because each refresh builds on the last. The gate isn't retried: a failed check is a data problem, and a retry would only send a second alert. Failures alert through the pipeline's own channel.
- **Dagster** (`orchestration/dagster/`): the same pipeline as software-defined assets. Raw tables map onto dbt sources, so lineage runs from the files to the KPIs. The gate checks are blocking asset checks, and the job uses the in-process executor because DuckDB allows one writer at a time.

title: CI
text:
### CI

GitHub Actions runs lint (Ruff, SQLFluff) and unit tests on every push. It then replays three monthly refreshes against the real data, runs the incremental-equivalence test, validates the Dagster definitions, builds dbt docs, and parses the Airflow DAG inside the real Airflow image. QC reports, alerts and the dbt docs site are uploaded as artifacts.

title: Portfolio assistant
text:
## Portfolio assistant

`chatbot/` is a small retrieval-augmented chatbot for recruiters and reviewers. `build_knowledge.py` turns this repository into about 60 passages: README sections, every dbt model's description, design note and tests, the gate checks and module docstrings. Questions are matched with BM25, and an open model on Hugging Face Inference Providers answers from the top passages only, citing the files. Without a token, the app shows the passages instead. A test fails CI if the docs change but the knowledge base isn't rebuilt. Deployment steps are in [chatbot/README.md](chatbot/README.md).

title: Repository layout
text:
## Repository layout

```
pipeline/                 ingest, load, quality gate, dbt runner, refresh QC, alerts, runner
transform/                dbt project: models, seeds, macros, generic and singular tests
orchestration/airflow/    DAG, Dockerfile, docker-compose
orchestration/dagster/    asset definitions
chatbot/                  Streamlit portfolio assistant for Hugging Face Spaces
tests/                    pytest: pipeline, QC, chatbot and the incremental-equivalence test
.github/workflows/ci.yml  lint, test, build, DAG parse
```

title: Data source and credits
text:
## Data source and credits

PKDD'99 Discovery Challenge financial dataset, prepared by Petr Berka and Marta Sochorova. The original host is offline, so the pipeline downloads the copy at [dnoeth/1999_Czech_financial_dataset_Teradata](https://github.com/dnoeth/1999_Czech_financial_dataset_Teradata), pinned to a commit. That copy shifts dates by 20 years (2013 to 2018), divides amounts by 10 and translates Czech codes into English abbreviations. No data is committed to this repository.

title: Model int_transactions_sequenced
text:
dbt model `int_transactions_sequenced` (layer: intermediate).
Transactions in recovered posting order, with the balance before each one and a continuity flag. The source has no posting time and its ids are not chronological, so the order is rebuilt from the running balance. See the model SQL for the rule.
Design note: Recovers the order in which transactions actually posted. The source has no posting time, and transaction_id is not chronological within a day, so ordering by (date, id) breaks the running balance on ~50% of rows. The bank posted credits before debits within a day; inside each group the reported balance itself gives the order (credits raise it, debits lower it). Ordering by (date, direction, balance path) reconciles all but a handful of 1.05M steps. Each row is then checked: previous balance + amount must equal the reported balance within a cent, because the mirror rounded amount and balance separately. Incremental: each run re-sequences the last `incremental_lookback_days` of every account plus anything new, and seeds the window from the last balance before it.
Materialization: incremental.
Column account_sequence: 1 for the account's first posting, then consecutive.
Column is_balance_continuous: Previous reported balance + amount equals this reported balance, within one cent.
Tests: unique_combination_of_columns; sequenced_transactions_reconcile_to_staging; sequenced_amounts_reconcile_to_staging; transaction_id: unique; transaction_id: not_null; account_sequence: not_null.

title: Model int_account_parties
text:
dbt model `int_account_parties` (layer: intermediate).
One row per account with its owner, optional disponent and highest-tier card.
Design note: Flattens the client-to-account bridge to one row per account: the owner, the optional disponent and the account's best card. Built here once so every mart joins accounts to people the same way and none of them fans out on dispositions.
Materialization: per folder default.
Tests: account_id: unique; account_id: not_null; account_id: relationships; owner_client_id: not_null.

title: Unit test same_day_postings_follow_the_balance_not_the_id
text: dbt unit test `same_day_postings_follow_the_balance_not_the_id` on `int_transactions_sequenced`. Ids 30 and 10 post on the same day as a credit and a debit. Credits post first, and the debit with the higher remaining balance comes before the lower one, whatever the ids say. Every step then reconciles.

title: Unit test a_one_cent_rounding_gap_is_continuous_two_cents_is_not
text: dbt unit test `a_one_cent_rounding_gap_is_continuous_two_cents_is_not` on `int_transactions_sequenced`.

title: Model dim_date
text:
dbt model `dim_date` (layer: core).
Calendar from 2013-01-01 to 2018-12-31.
Design note: Calendar dimension. Built with a recursive CTE so it compiles unchanged on DuckDB and Snowflake; no package dependency.
Materialization: per folder default.
Tests: date_day: unique; date_day: not_null.

title: Model dim_district
text:
dbt model `dim_district` (layer: core).
Districts with demographics and a capital, urban or rural type.

title: Model dim_client
text:
dbt model `dim_client` (layer: core).
Clients with age at the end of the observed period and home region.
Materialization: per folder default.
Column age_at_period_end: Age at the end of the observed period. Junior-account disponents can be young children.
Tests: client_id: unique; client_id: not_null; age_at_period_end: expression_is_true.

title: Model dim_account
text:
dbt model `dim_account` (layer: core).
Account dimension. Flattens owner, disponent, best card, loan and standing orders to one row per account, so facts join to it without fanning out.
Materialization: per folder default.
Tests: dim_account_has_every_staged_account; account_id: unique; account_id: not_null; owner_client_id: not_null; owner_client_id: relationships; branch_district_id: relationships.

title: Model fct_transactions
text:
dbt model `fct_transactions` (layer: core).
Transaction fact at posting grain, incremental, with decoded codes and recovered posting order.
Design note: Transaction fact at posting grain, with codes decoded through the seed. Incremental: only the lookback window and new postings are rewritten on each run.
Materialization: incremental.
Tests: unique_combination_of_columns; fct_transactions_reconcile_to_staging; transaction_id: unique; transaction_id: not_null; account_id: relationships; posted_on: relationships; transaction_type: not_null; credit_amount: expression_is_true.

title: Model fct_account_monthly
text:
dbt model `fct_account_monthly` (layer: core).
Account-month snapshot from opening to the last month of data, including quiet months. Opening balance is last month's closing; closing is the bank's reported balance.
Design note: Periodic snapshot fact: one row per account per month from the month it opened to the last month in the data, including months with no activity (balance carried forward). Closing balance is the bank's reported balance after the month's last posting, not a running sum, so it never drifts. Opening balance is the previous month's closing. `rounding_adjustment` is what is left after opening + net flow; the mirror rounds amounts and balances separately, so it is a few cents at most, and a test bounds it.
Materialization: per folder default.
Tests: unique_combination_of_columns; monthly_flows_reconcile_to_transactions; monthly_rounding_adjustment_is_cents; closing_balance: not_null; account_id: relationships.

title: Model mart_monthly_kpis
text:
dbt model `mart_monthly_kpis` (layer: reporting).
Board-level monthly KPIs, one row per month. The refresh-over-refresh QC snapshots this table after every run and compares it with the previous refresh.
Design note: Board-level monthly KPIs. One row per month. This is the table the refresh-over-refresh QC compares between runs: closed months must not move, and the newest month must sit inside its expected band. The contract stops a refactor from silently renaming or retyping a reported column.
Materialization: per folder default.
Contract: enforced (column names and types are fixed).
Tests: kpi_deposits_reconcile_to_account_months; kpi_transactions_reconcile_to_fact; month_start: unique; active_accounts: expression_is_true.

title: Model fct_loans
text:
dbt model `fct_loans` (layer: risk).
One row per loan with status, risk flags, ledger repayments and estimated outstanding principal.
Design note: One row per loan with its status, risk flags, repayments seen in the ledger and an outstanding-principal estimate. The contract fixes names and types, because risk and regulatory reporting read this table directly.
Materialization: per folder default.
Contract: enforced (column names and types are fixed).
Tests: loan_id: unique; account_id: unique; account_id: relationships; principal_amount: expression_is_true; risk_bucket: accepted_values; outstanding_principal: expression_is_true.

Design note: Loan book by vintage and region: the grain a credit-risk committee reviews. Default rate counts loans in status B (written off) or D (in arrears).
Materialization: per folder default.
Tests: unique_combination_of_columns; portfolio_principal_reconciles_to_loans; default_rate_is_a_share.

title: Singular test assert_balance_continuity
text: dbt singular test `assert_balance_continuity`. The ledger must reconcile: every posting's previous balance plus its amount equals the balance the bank reported. A handful of same-day ties cannot be ordered from the data alone, so the test warns on any break and fails the build only if breaks exceed `balance_break_error_share` of postings, which would mean the sequencing logic, or the source, is wrong.

title: Singular test assert_fct_transactions_reconcile_to_raw
text: dbt singular test `assert_fct_transactions_reconcile_to_raw`. End-to-end reconciliation: per month, the published fact must hold exactly the rows and the money that arrived in raw. Any difference means a model dropped, duplicated or mis-typed a posting somewhere between landing and the mart.

title: Quality gate checks
text:
The quality gate runs on the raw layer before any dbt model is rebuilt. BLOCK checks stop the pipeline so marts keep the last good build; ALERT checks notify and let the run continue.
G01 Every raw table has rows (BLOCK): An empty table means the extract or the load failed silently.
G02 Transaction ids are unique (BLOCK): A duplicated posting would double money in every downstream total.
G03 Dates and amounts parse (BLOCK): Unparseable values mean the file layout changed upstream.
G04 Every posting has an account (BLOCK): Orphan postings would silently drop out of every account-level mart.
G05 No closed month is empty (BLOCK): A gap in the monthly series means a partition was missed.
G06 Feed is current (ALERT): Latest posting should be within a few days of the extract date.
G07 Volume band (ALERT): Latest closed month within 25% of the median of the six months before it.
G08 Blank category share (ALERT): Uncategorised postings normally run near 51%; a jump means a mapping broke upstream.

title: Code: pipeline/dbt_step.py
text:
Run dbt programmatically, so every orchestrator calls dbt the same way.

Usage:
    python -m pipeline.dbt_step --select "staging intermediate"
    python -m pipeline.dbt_step --select marts --full-refresh

title: Code: pipeline/ingest.py
text:
Extract: download the source files and verify them against a checksum lock.

Each file is fetched from a pinned commit, streamed to a temp file and only moved
into the landing zone once its SHA-256 matches the lock. A changed upstream file
therefore fails loudly here instead of silently changing every number downstream.

Usage:
    python -m pipeline.ingest            # download what is missing, verify all
    python -m pipeline.ingest --relock   # accept current upstream bytes as the new lock

title: Code: pipeline/load.py
text:
Load: land the verified files in the warehouse `raw` schema, exactly as received.

Raw tables keep every column as text, so a bad value in the source never breaks the
load; typing and cleaning happen in dbt staging, where failures are tested and visible.

The source is a static 1993-1998 extract. To exercise incremental models, freshness
checks and refresh-over-refresh QC the way a live feed would, the loader can replay it:
`--as-of 2016-06-30` emits only the rows whose business date is on or before that day,
like a source system extracted on that date. Without `--as-of` the full history loads.

Usage:
    python -m pipeline.load                    # full history
    python -m pipeline.load --as-of 2016-06-30 # simulated extract as of a date

title: Code: pipeline/notify.py
text:
Alerts: every run outcome and failed check reaches a person, not just a log.

Channels are configured by environment variable only:

* SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL               post to a Slack incoming webhook
* SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, ALERT_EMAIL_TO, ALERT_EMAIL_FROM
                                  send an email

With nothing configured, alerts are only appended to `logs/alerts.jsonl`, so local runs
and CI never message anyone. A failed send is logged and recorded, never raised: an alert
problem must not take the pipeline down with it.

title: Code: pipeline/quality_gate.py
text:
Quality gate: checks the raw layer before any model is rebuilt.

A load that finishes is not a load that is right. Each check is either:

* BLOCK - the data is wrong in a way no model can fix. The gate exits non-zero, the
  orchestrator skips every downstream task, and the marts keep the last good build:
  stale, but not wrong.
* ALERT - something moved that a person should look at, but the data is usable. The
  result is recorded and an alert is sent; the run continues.

Every result is stored in `dq.check_results`, so any morning can be replayed. To let one
run through on purpose, insert a row into `dq.gate_bypass` for the check and as-of date.

Usage:
    python -m pipeline.quality_gate --as-of 2016-06-30

title: Code: pipeline/refresh_compare.py
Code: pipeline/run.py
text:
Run the whole pipeline once, in order, without an orchestrator.

    extract -> load raw -> quality gate -> dbt staging + intermediate -> dbt marts -> refresh QC

Airflow and Dagster call the same step functions; this module is the reference order and
what CI runs. A BLOCK in the gate stops the run before any model is rebuilt.

Usage:
    python -m pipeline.run                       # full history
    python -m pipeline.run --as-of 2016-06-30    # simulated extract
    python -m pipeline.run --replay 2016-01-31 2016-06-30   # one refresh per month-end

title: Code: orchestration/airflow/dags/bank_monthly_refresh.py
text:
Monthly refresh of the bank data platform.

One DAG run per month-end. With catchup on, Airflow backfills 2016-2018 as a series of
monthly refreshes: each run extracts the source as of its month-end, so the incremental
models, the quality gate and the refresh-over-refresh QC run exactly as on a live feed.

    ingest -> load_raw -> quality_gate -> dbt_staging -> dbt_marts -> refresh_qc

The pipeline runs in its own virtualenv inside the image (BANK_PYTHON), so dbt's
dependencies never clash with Airflow's. A BLOCK in the gate fails its task and Airflow
skips everything downstream: the marts keep last month's build.

title: Code: orchestration/dagster/bank_dagster/definitions.py
text:
Dagster version of the pipeline: the same steps as software-defined assets.

Where Airflow schedules tasks, Dagster models the data: every raw table and every dbt
model is an asset with lineage, and the quality gate is a set of blocking asset checks on
the raw tables, so a failed check stops downstream materialisation.

    dagster dev -m bank_dagster.definitions      (from orchestration/dagster)

No `from __future__ import annotations` here: Dagster reads the Config type hints at runtime.

title: Chatbot: Portfolio assistant
text:
# Portfolio assistant

A Streamlit chatbot that answers questions about the [bank data platform](../README.md): how it was modelled, tested and orchestrated, and why.

title: Chatbot: How it works
text:
## How it works

1. **Knowledge base from the code.** `build_knowledge.py` turns the repository into about 60 passages: README sections, every dbt model's description, design note and tests, the quality-gate checks, module docstrings, and the hand-written `knowledge/*.md` files. Each passage records its source file.
2. **Retrieval.** Each question, plus the previous question so follow-ups keep their topic, is matched against the passages with BM25 (`retrieval.py`). Keyword matching suits a small technical corpus full of exact identifiers, and it needs no embedding model or vector store.
3. **Grounded generation.** The top passages go to an open model on Hugging Face Inference Providers (default `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, with two fallbacks). The model is instructed to answer only from them, cite the files, never invent figures or experience, and treat the context as data, not instructions.
4. **Graceful degradation.** Without `HF_TOKEN`, or if every model is unavailable, the app shows the most relevant passages instead of failing.

title: Chatbot: Run locally
text:
## Run locally

```bash
uv sync --extra chatbot
uv run python chatbot/build_knowledge.py
uv run streamlit run chatbot/app.py
```

Set `HF_TOKEN` to enable generated answers. Without it you get retrieval-only answers.

title: Chatbot: Deploy to Hugging Face Spaces
text:
## Deploy to Hugging Face Spaces

1. Fill in `knowledge/about_me.md`, then rebuild the knowledge base with `python chatbot/build_knowledge.py`. Sections still marked TODO are left out, and the bot will say it doesn't know.
2. Create a Space with the **Docker** SDK.
3. Push the contents of this `chatbot/` folder to the Space repository: `app.py`, `retrieval.py`, `requirements.txt`, `Dockerfile`, this `README.md` and `knowledge/chunks.jsonl`.
4. In the Space settings, add the secret `HF_TOKEN`, a fine-grained token with the "Make calls to Inference Providers" permission. Optionally add the variables `REPO_URL` (your GitHub repo, used for source links) and `HF_MODEL`.

Inference Providers usage is billed to the token's account, with a free monthly allowance.

title: Why this dataset?
text:
## Why this dataset?

The PKDD'99 Czech bank dataset is one of the very few public datasets with a real bank ledger: accounts, clients, loans, cards and over a million transactions with running balances. It is messy in realistic ways: padded and blank codes, missing demographics, no posting time and non-chronological ids. That made it a good stand-in for the platform data an analytics engineer at a bank would model.

title: Why DuckDB instead of Snowflake?
text:
## Why DuckDB instead of Snowflake?

DuckDB lets anyone clone the repo and run the whole warehouse on a laptop or in CI for free. The dbt project uses dbt's cross-database macros (dateadd, date_trunc, datediff, last_day) and a recursive CTE for the calendar, so the same SQL compiles on Snowflake. The profile includes a Snowflake target that reads credentials from environment variables. It is not exercised in CI.

title: Why both Airflow and Dagster?
text:
## Why both Airflow and Dagster?

To show the same pipeline in the two most common orchestration styles. Airflow schedules tasks: a monthly DAG with catchup replays 2016 to 2018 as monthly refreshes. Dagster models data assets: raw tables, every dbt model and the QC step are assets with lineage, and the quality gate is a set of blocking asset checks. Both call the same Python step functions, so neither has its own copy of the logic.

title: Why write custom generic tests instead of using dbt_utils?
text:
## Why write custom generic tests instead of using dbt_utils?

The project needs no package downloads, so it builds anywhere. The three generic tests (`expression_is_true`, `unique_combination_of_columns`, `reconciles_with`) are short and show how dbt tests work under the hood. `reconciles_with` is the important one: it compares a sum or count between two relations, overall or per group, with a tolerance. That is how every layer reconciles to the layer before it.

title: How do you know the incremental models are right?
text:
## How do you know the incremental models are right?

`tests/test_incremental_equivalence.py` loads two month-end extracts, builds the second one incrementally, fingerprints the incremental tables (row count plus an order-independent hash of every column), then rebuilds from scratch and asserts the fingerprints are identical. The refresh-over-refresh QC also confirms that closed months never change between replayed refreshes.

title: What would you do next?
text:
## What would you do next?

- Add a mart-level check of each published table against its source in the gate, not only in dbt tests.
- Replace the fixed 25% volume band with a seasonal baseline.
- Add SCD type 2 snapshots once a source with changing attributes is available. This dataset is a single extract, so nothing changes over time.
- Run the Snowflake target in CI against a trial account.
